Analyze the following external review feedback and check how it was addressed.
You have tools available — use `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- ':(exclude).planwerk'` to see ALL changes on this feature branch. You can also read individual files.

Generate a JSON object with:
- "resolution_summary": A concise summary (2-4 sentences) of what was done overall to address the review.
- "comment_resolutions": An array of strings, one per code comment (in the same order), each describing what was changed at that location. If there are no code comments, return an empty array.

IMPORTANT: If changes were made to files or locations NOT directly mentioned in the review feedback, the resolution_summary MUST explicitly list these additional changes and explain WHY they were necessary (e.g., 'Applied new pattern X from reviewer comment to N additional matching locations: [list files]'). This makes broad changes traceable to the original review comment.

## Review Feedback
Hey - I've found 2 issues, and left some high level feedback:

- The updated owner-ref path in secretToKeystoneMapper now matches only on Kind and exact APIVersion, dropping the previous UID-based isOwnedBy check; consider either retaining a UID-based match or at least accepting any version in the keystone.openstack.c5c3.io group so existing Secrets continue to map correctly across version bumps.
- secretToKeystoneMapper currently enqueues reconcile requests purely from ownerReferences without verifying that the referenced Keystone objects actually exist; if spurious or stale ownerRefs are a concern, you may want to guard this with an existence check or a lightweight cache lookup to avoid queuing work for non-existent CRs.

The blank identifier ignores errors from `keystonePaths()`. If it fails (for example, when the CRD directory is missing), envtest will later error in a less obvious way. Here, "producing API-server load" could be updated to "producing API server load" to better match Kubernetes documentation conventions.

Suggested implementation:

```
Without the indexer, every Secret create/update/delete event in a namespace
containing ESO-managed Secrets would force the mapper to List every Keystone CR
in that namespace — producing API server load that scales linearly with the
number of Secret events, not with the number of Keystone CRs (CC-0087, REQ-001).

```

You may want to run a project-wide search for "API-server" and similarly update any other occurrences to "API server" for consistency across the documentation.
